question.problem: Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ Find the likelihood function of the sample $2.1,\,5.0,\,4.2,\,1.4.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}\theta {e}^{-\theta {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-\theta \sum {x}_{i}} \\  & ={\theta }^{n}\,{e}^{-S\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$ 

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =2.1+5.0+4.2+1.4 \\  & =12.7\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\theta }^{4}\,{e}^{-12.7\theta }.\end{aligned}
$$
